title: Feature commencement heatmap and acceptance criteria
body:
Context and goal:
This is a compact operational artifact intended to convert an engineering + product roadmap slice into a clear, two-week cadence heatmap tied directly to go/no-go acceptance criteria and prioritized KPIs. It’s optimized for mid-stage features where stakeholders need a lightweight but actionable decision surface for rollout gating and early incident playbooks.

How to use this sheet (quick guide):
- Run at the start of each two-week sprint during planning.
- Populate milestone lanes (design, infra, e2e, docs, cs enablement) with color codes: green (on track), amber (risk), red (blocked).
- Explicitly list the owner and primary acceptance criterion per lane; acceptance is binary for gating decisions but include notes for partial acceptance paths.
- Capture 3 priority KPIs for the feature and the threshold that must be met by pilot week 2 to continue rollout.
- Record contingency triggers (what to do when threshold violated) and autoresponse owner.

Section A — Cadence heatmap (visualized as row entries in the sheet):
Columns: Week-start date | Feature | Design | Infra | Integration | E2E QA | Docs | CS Training | Release Flag (Y/N) | Owner | Acceptance criterion (pass/fail) | Notes
Example row (fill-in):
- 2025-11-17 | Smart-routing v2 | Green | Amber | Amber | Amber | Green | Amber | N | Priya K. | 95th p95 latency <= 200ms on staging + no regression in top-20 intents | Infra autoscaler needs param tuning; plan to ship canary with 10% traffic later if infra green in week 2.

Guidance for heatmap statuses:
- Green = All required tasks completed or actively gated with low risk; no unmitigated dependencies.
- Amber = Work in progress with known risks that have mitigation owners and timelines.
- Red = Blocked by an unresolved dependency or critical bug; escalate to triage lead.

Section B — Acceptance criteria template (one row per lane)
- Lane: [e.g., Integration]
- Owner: [name]
- Criterion: [concise binary test or checklist, e.g., "end-to-end flow for principal 3 intents completes with correct output in <=2s on staging"]
- Test harness: [unit/e2e/manual + ticket id or script link]
- Roll decision: Proceed / Delay / Rollback if fail
- Partial path: [if any functionality can be toggled off and still ship]

Section C — KPI prioritizer (feature-specific, pick up to 3):
Columns: KPI name | Rationale | Baseline | Pilot threshold (week 2) | Owner | Measurement method | Escalation action if unmet
Example entries:
- Successful-response-rate (SRR) | Core user success signal | 0.87 | >=0.90 | Diego M. | Prod logs + sampling | Pause rollout; open top-10 failure ticket; hotfix sprint
- Median latency (ms) | UX snappiness | 320 | <=250 | Ethan P. | Tracing + CI load tests | Scale workers + enable shorter-context model variant
- Token cost per session | Unit economics | $0.65 | <=$0.50 | Ava C. | Billing + sampling | Enable caching + quantized model for pilot cohort

Scoring and prioritization heuristic (how we pick which KPI to act on first):
- Severity (impact on customer experience) x Likelihood (observed regression vs baseline) x Operational cost to remediate.
- We weigh severity double for safety/security signals (e.g., PII leakage) and triple for revenue-impacting regressions.
- Use score to sequence mitigation work in the immediate 48-hour window.

Section D — Contingency playbook snippets (short, copyable actions):
- Infra overload (p95 > 500ms, error rate > 2%): Throttle non-critical routes, route premium users to fallback model, spin emergency infra pool (owner: infra oncall).
- SRR drop (>=5% below threshold): Disable experimental ranking feature, revert to prior model weights, engage solutions eng for root cause.
- Docs/guides incomplete at ship: Mark feature as "beta docs" and include in CS triage; shift CS training to weekly live Q&A rather than full-runbook for first two weeks.

Section E — Launch gating checklist (binary checks; all must be green to flip Release Flag to Y):
1) Top acceptance criterion for each lane marked PASS (owner signoff).
2) All priority KPIs have measurement pipelines validated and dashboards up.
3) Incident runbook created and reachable (link).
4) Rollback path validated (feature toggle + traffic split).
5) CS and comms have at least one dry-run with sample responses.
6) Legal/compliance checks passed for data handling (if applicable).

Quick template for decision minutes (first 48 hours after pilot):
- Pilot cohort size and date/time window
- Observed KPI deltas vs baseline (list numbers)
- Any amber/red lanes and mitigation started (owner + ETA)
- Decision: widen / hold / rollback (owner for final call)

Appendix — suggested dashboard widgets to create before pilot:
- KPI sparkline for the 3 priority KPIs (1h resolution)
- Error-rate by intent + example failure sample (linked to ticket)
- Latency distribution with 95/99th markers and service maps
- Cost per session trends and projection for 30d scale

Notes and open questions (captured during working sessions):
- Consider building a small synthetic probe that runs the top-5 intents every 10 minutes to catch regressions earlier.
- For quantization-related cost improvements, document quality delta on a curated human eval set prior to enabling in pilot.
- Need to decide whether canary traffic should be weighted by region for geopolitical latency sensitivity testing.

Ownership and cadence commitments:
- Product Ops (Ava Chen) maintains the sheet and runs gating syncs.
- Engineering owners update lane statuses by Friday 10:00am PST each sprint.
- Triage lead (rotating) will convene an immediate 30-minute session if any lane flips to red.

Last notes: this sheet is purposely minimal — the objective is to create a defensible, auditable decision surface for the first two weeks of a rollout and to make remediation decisions deterministic. Keep entries short, link to deeper artifacts rather than copying long docs here.
